newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Amcol not reporting half-year results.
newsitem.headline: Amcol not reporting half-year results.

text.p: Troubled property and trading group Amcol Holdings will not report results for the six months ended June 30 because investigations into the company's affairs are not complete, its judicial managers said on Friday.

"In the light of this, we are not in a position to submit the half-yearly report and shall not be doing so," judicial manager Yeoh Oon Jin said in a statement to the Stock Exchange of Singapore (SES), made available to Reuters on Friday.
Companies listed on the SES are required to publish their interim results no later than three months after their first half financial year.

Judicial managers from Price Waterhouse, at the request of the SES, were appointed by the High Court on August 30 to carry out a thorough investigation into the collapse of Amcol and write an official report on the affair.
Amcol was placed under interim judicial management in July after a Price Waterhouse report said the company had serious cashflow problems and had diffculty meeting its financial obligations.

In August, the judicial managers announced an agreement with Indonesian conglomerate Sinar Mas group to rescue Amcol through the creation of a new company into which Sinar Mas would inject at least US$2.0 billion in assets.
